reason: Conversation 1 gathers more useful evidence: it has the customer check the impeller by hand with the power off and then asks about the display code. That surfaces E18 and the stiff, gritty impeller. Its weaknesses are that it treats FD 9409 as the model number and tells the customer to quote it to Bosch, and it concludes 'you will need to replace the drain pump' a bit too confidently while still noting the sump hose is unchecked. Conversation 2 has a garbled, self-contradictory reply (a 'Likely cause: drain pump' heading followed by 'No, it is not most likely the pump'). It never asks for the display code or model, never has the impeller checked properly, and also treats FD 9409 as the model. It mostly just hands the job to an engineer, though its unplug-first safety note is good.
